decisionNodes.stem: What initial management should you recommend for this patient now?

answerChoices.label: Incision and drainage with empiric antibiotics
Surgical excision of the involved superficial vein

decisionNodes.explanation: Concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease is generally self-limited. Initial care is supportive with warm compresses, an NSAID when appropriate, avoidance of irritating activity or clothing, and follow-up. Antibiotics, venous excision, and therapeutic anticoagulation are not routine without a separate indication.

decisionNodes.stem: How should the clinic handle the treating specialist's relevant information request after Ethan Kingston authorizes Mondor-disease care coordination?

answerChoices.label: Share relevant information for authorized care
answerChoices.rationale: The patient has authorized coordination, and the specialist requests relevant information. Share for that purpose while avoiding unnecessary disclosure.

answerChoices.label: Request a new authorization for each relevant chart item
answerChoices.rationale: The supplied authorization already supports relevant coordination. Treating every relevant item as newly prohibited obstructs that authorized care purpose.

answerChoices.label: Send the complete chart for the specialist to filter
answerChoices.rationale: The whole chart may include information beyond the consultation's purpose. Authorization to coordinate does not justify unnecessary disclosure for the specialist to filter later.

answerChoices.label: Send a de-identified summary for the treating consultation
answerChoices.rationale: The specialist needs relevant patient-specific consultation information. A de-identified substitute does not provide the authorized coordination requested in this scenario.

decisionNodes.explanation: Share relevant patient-specific information for the authorized consultation, avoiding unnecessary disclosure. The stated authorization supports that coordination; confidentiality does not require blocking every exchange or sending the entire chart.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Confidentiality permits appropriate exchange for authorized care; it does not prohibit all coordination. Share information relevant to the consultation while avoiding unnecessary disclosure. Remember to match the information to its purpose. Sending the whole chart for someone else to filter, or treating every relevant item as newly forbidden, misses that balance in this supplied setting.
sourceLabels: Mondor's Disease: A Review of the Literature

decisionNodes.explanation: Offer supportive care for concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease, including warm compresses, an NSAID when appropriate and follow-up. Other treatments require a separate indication.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease is generally self-limited. Initial care is supportive with warm compresses, an NSAID when appropriate, avoidance of irritating activity or clothing, and follow-up. Antibiotics, venous excision, and therapeutic anticoagulation are not routine without a separate indication.

decisionNodes.stem: What initial management should you recommend for this patient now?

answerChoices.label: Incision and drainage with empiric antibiotics
Surgical excision of the involved superficial vein

decisionNodes.explanation: Concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease is generally self-limited. Initial care is supportive with warm compresses, an NSAID when appropriate, avoidance of irritating activity or clothing, and follow-up. Antibiotics, venous excision, and therapeutic anticoagulation are not routine without a separate indication.

decisionNodes.stem: How should the clinic handle the treating specialist's relevant information request after Ethan Kingston authorizes Mondor-disease care coordination?

answerChoices.label: Share relevant information for authorized care
answerChoices.rationale: The patient has authorized coordination, and the specialist requests relevant information. Share for that purpose while avoiding unnecessary disclosure.

answerChoices.label: Request a new authorization for each relevant chart item
answerChoices.rationale: The supplied authorization already supports relevant coordination. Treating every relevant item as newly prohibited obstructs that authorized care purpose.

answerChoices.label: Send the complete chart for the specialist to filter
answerChoices.rationale: The whole chart may include information beyond the consultation's purpose. Authorization to coordinate does not justify unnecessary disclosure for the specialist to filter later.

answerChoices.label: Send a de-identified summary for the treating consultation
answerChoices.rationale: The specialist needs relevant patient-specific consultation information. A de-identified substitute does not provide the authorized coordination requested in this scenario.

decisionNodes.explanation: Share relevant patient-specific information for the authorized consultation, avoiding unnecessary disclosure. The stated authorization supports that coordination; confidentiality does not require blocking every exchange or sending the entire chart.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Confidentiality permits appropriate exchange for authorized care; it does not prohibit all coordination. Share information relevant to the consultation while avoiding unnecessary disclosure. Remember to match the information to its purpose. frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the breast-service research lead, reviews a trial of a new topical agent after drainage of lactational breast abscesses. Different participants received each preparation. Ultrasound measured the remaining cavity area at the protocol visit. A colleague proposes linking the groups because the same sonographer collected all measurements. The report includes the distribution checks for analysis.
sourceLabels: ACR Appropriateness Criteria Breast Imaging During Lactation
Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine Clinical Protocol #36: The Mastitis Spectrum, Revised 2022

decisionNodes.stem: Which analysis best fits the study's comparison of mean remaining abscess-cavity area, using the measurements and assumptions in the exhibit?

answerChoices.label: Two-sample t test
answerChoices.rationale: The study compares means from two groups of different people, and its stated continuous-data assumptions are reasonable. A two-sample t procedure matches that structure.

answerChoices.label: Wilcoxon rank-sum test
answerChoices.rationale: Rank-sum answers a ranked-observation comparison. This study explicitly requests means and supplies reasonable assumptions for the mean-based procedure.

answerChoices.label: Chi-square test of independence
answerChoices.rationale: Chi-square testing analyzes counts in categories. The requested comparison concerns continuous measurements or ordered ratings, not a categorical contingency table.

answerChoices.label: Paired t test
answerChoices.rationale: A paired t procedure needs repeated or deliberately matched measurements. This comparison does not supply those links between observations.

decisionNodes.explanation: A two-sample t test fits mean remaining abscess-cavity area in two nonoverlapping groups. Using the same sonographer does not create repeated or matched observations.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: The scanner does not define the relationship between observations. These abscess-cavity areas come from different people in two nonoverlapping groups, with suitable continuous-data assumptions. A two-sample t test compares their means. Remember to ask who was measured, not whether the groups used the same instrument or had the same number of columns.

exhibit.title: Remaining abscess-cavity area — illustrative clinical study
exhibit.body: Invented protocol observations for an unnamed investigational topical agent in lactational breast abscesses. Outcome: remaining abscess-cavity area, in square centimeters. Two separately sampled treatment groups contribute one measurement per person. Groups do not overlap and nobody is matched. Measurements are approximately normal with comparable variability and no influential outliers. These practice assumptions supply no real treatment efficacy.

decisionNodes.stem: What should the team explain when Colin Lennox is told that ordinary gastric-GIST care depends on joining an optional new-biologic study?

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment postpones the surgical consultation
answerChoices.rationale: Postponing the ordinary consultation because enrollment is declined still makes care conditional on joining. That conflicts with voluntary choice in this setting.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment requires transfer to another clinic
answerChoices.rationale: Requiring transfer would impose a loss of ordinary care for declining this optional study. The scenario gives no basis for making that care contingent on enrollment.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment limits access to routine follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Limiting routine follow-up uses ordinary care to pressure enrollment. The optional study is not required for that care.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment does not forfeit ordinary care
answerChoices.rationale: This study is optional and not required for ordinary care. Clarify that declining enrollment does not forfeit that care, so the invitation can be considered voluntarily.

decisionNodes.explanation: Clarify that declining this optional study does not forfeit ordinary clinic care. The recruiter's stated condition is inconsistent with voluntary participation in a study not required for that care.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Research participation must be voluntary. When a study is optional and not required for ordinary care, declining it should not forfeit that care. Remember to separate the clinical care decision from the research invitation. Making enrollment a condition of routine care pressures the patient instead of supporting an independent choice about participation.

decisionNodes.stem: Which multidisciplinary treatment plan best fits Colin Lennox's imatinib-sensitive, nonmetastatic gastric GIST when tumor shrinkage could reduce the morbidity of the planned extensive resection?

answerChoices.label: Offer symptom-directed care without tumor treatment
answerChoices.rationale: Symptom-only care does not address this large, locally advanced lesion.

answerChoices.label: Plan neoadjuvant imatinib before reassessing resection
answerChoices.rationale: For an imatinib-sensitive GIST where the multidisciplinary team expects shrinkage to reduce operative morbidity, neoadjuvant imatinib with later resection reassessment is appropriate; size alone would not establish this plan.

answerChoices.label: Give neoadjuvant cytotoxic chemotherapy before resection
answerChoices.rationale: Conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy is not the selected targeted approach for imatinib-sensitive GIST.

answerChoices.label: Proceed directly to the planned extensive resection
answerChoices.rationale: Immediate extensive surgery gives up the documented opportunity for morbidity-reducing shrinkage.

decisionNodes.explanation: Plan neoadjuvant imatinib with later reassessment of resection for this mutation-sensitive GIST. The documented opportunity to reduce operative morbidity supports the plan; size alone does not.

decisionNodes.stem: Which change should be requested in Sabrina Russo's draft report?

answerChoices.label: Retain the reserve conclusion; revise the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: This accepts suppression as proof of reserve and lets symptom reproduction override the actual junction and pressure observations during loading.

answerChoices.label: Revise the reserve conclusion; revise the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: The reserve conclusion needs correction, but the symptom-provoking liquid load does not itself supply evidence for the added outflow revision.

decisionNodes.explanation: A tender, taut superficial cord along the anterolateral breast or chest wall is characteristic of Mondor disease, which is superficial thrombophlebitis. frozenCase.displayName: Select an independent-samples t test and Select a paired t test
frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the breast-service research lead, reviews a trial of a new topical agent after drainage of lactational breast abscesses. Different participants received each preparation. Ultrasound measured the remaining cavity area at the protocol visit. A colleague proposes linking the groups because the same sonographer collected all measurements. The report includes the distribution checks for analysis.
sourceLabels: ACR Appropriateness Criteria Breast Imaging During Lactation
Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine Clinical Protocol #36: The Mastitis Spectrum, Revised 2022

decisionNodes.stem: Which analysis best fits the study's comparison of mean remaining abscess-cavity area, using the measurements and assumptions in the exhibit?

answerChoices.label: Two-sample t test
answerChoices.rationale: The study compares means from two groups of different people, and its stated continuous-data assumptions are reasonable. A two-sample t procedure matches that structure.

answerChoices.label: Wilcoxon rank-sum test
answerChoices.rationale: Rank-sum answers a ranked-observation comparison. This study explicitly requests means and supplies reasonable assumptions for the mean-based procedure.

answerChoices.label: Chi-square test of independence
answerChoices.rationale: Chi-square testing analyzes counts in categories. The requested comparison concerns continuous measurements or ordered ratings, not a categorical contingency table.

answerChoices.label: Paired t test
answerChoices.rationale: A paired t procedure needs repeated or deliberately matched measurements. This comparison does not supply those links between observations.

decisionNodes.explanation: A two-sample t test fits mean remaining abscess-cavity area in two nonoverlapping groups. Using the same sonographer does not create repeated or matched observations.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: The scanner does not define the relationship between observations. These abscess-cavity areas come from different people in two nonoverlapping groups, with suitable continuous-data assumptions. A two-sample t test compares their means. Remember to ask who was measured, not whether the groups used the same instrument or had the same number of columns.

exhibit.title: Remaining abscess-cavity area — illustrative clinical study
exhibit.body: Invented protocol observations for an unnamed investigational topical agent in lactational breast abscesses. Outcome: remaining abscess-cavity area, in square centimeters. Two separately sampled treatment groups contribute one measurement per person. Groups do not overlap and nobody is matched. Measurements are approximately normal with comparable variability and no influential outliers. These practice assumptions supply no real treatment efficacy.

decisionNodes.stem: What should the team explain when Colin Lennox is told that ordinary gastric-GIST care depends on joining an optional new-biologic study?

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment postpones the surgical consultation
answerChoices.rationale: Postponing the ordinary consultation because enrollment is declined still makes care conditional on joining. That conflicts with voluntary choice in this setting.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment requires transfer to another clinic
answerChoices.rationale: Requiring transfer would impose a loss of ordinary care for declining this optional study. The scenario gives no basis for making that care contingent on enrollment.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment limits access to routine follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Limiting routine follow-up uses ordinary care to pressure enrollment. The optional study is not required for that care.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment does not forfeit ordinary care
answerChoices.rationale: This study is optional and not required for ordinary care. Clarify that declining enrollment does not forfeit that care, so the invitation can be considered voluntarily.

decisionNodes.explanation: Clarify that declining this optional study does not forfeit ordinary clinic care. The recruiter's stated condition is inconsistent with voluntary participation in a study not required for that care.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Research participation must be voluntary. When a study is optional and not required for ordinary care, declining it should not forfeit that care. Remember to separate the clinical care decision from the research invitation. Making enrollment a condition of routine care pressures the patient instead of supporting an independent choice about participation.
sourceLabels: 2023 GEIS Guidelines for gastrointestinal stromal tumors
Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors Treatment (PDQ®), Health Professional Version

decisionNodes.stem: Which multidisciplinary treatment plan best fits Colin Lennox's imatinib-sensitive, nonmetastatic gastric GIST when tumor shrinkage could reduce the morbidity of the planned extensive resection?

answerChoices.label: Offer symptom-directed care without tumor treatment

answerChoices.label: Plan neoadjuvant imatinib before reassessing resection
answerChoices.rationale: For an imatinib-sensitive GIST where the multidisciplinary team expects shrinkage to reduce operative morbidity, neoadjuvant imatinib with later resection reassessment is appropriate; size alone would not establish this plan.

answerChoices.label: Give neoadjuvant cytotoxic chemotherapy before resection
answerChoices.rationale: Conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy is not the selected targeted approach for imatinib-sensitive GIST.

answerChoices.label: Proceed directly to the planned extensive resection
answerChoices.rationale: Immediate extensive surgery gives up the documented opportunity for morbidity-reducing shrinkage.

frozenCase.displayName: Select an independent-samples t test and Select a paired t test
frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the breast-service research lead, reviews a trial of a new topical agent after drainage of lactational breast abscesses. Different participants received each preparation. Ultrasound measured the remaining cavity area at the protocol visit. A colleague proposes linking the groups because the same sonographer collected all measurements. The report includes the distribution checks for analysis.
sourceLabels: ACR Appropriateness Criteria Breast Imaging During Lactation
Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine Clinical Protocol #36: The Mastitis Spectrum, Revised 2022

decisionNodes.stem: Which analysis best fits the study's comparison of mean remaining abscess-cavity area, using the measurements and assumptions in the exhibit?

answerChoices.label: Two-sample t test
answerChoices.rationale: The study compares means from two groups of different people, and its stated continuous-data assumptions are reasonable. A two-sample t procedure matches that structure.

answerChoices.label: Wilcoxon rank-sum test
answerChoices.rationale: Rank-sum answers a ranked-observation comparison. This study explicitly requests means and supplies reasonable assumptions for the mean-based procedure.

answerChoices.label: Chi-square test of independence
answerChoices.rationale: Chi-square testing analyzes counts in categories. The requested comparison concerns continuous measurements or ordered ratings, not a categorical contingency table.

answerChoices.label: Paired t test
answerChoices.rationale: A paired t procedure needs repeated or deliberately matched measurements. This comparison does not supply those links between observations.

decisionNodes.explanation: A two-sample t test fits mean remaining abscess-cavity area in two nonoverlapping groups. Using the same sonographer does not create repeated or matched observations.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: The scanner does not define the relationship between observations. These abscess-cavity areas come from different people in two nonoverlapping groups, with suitable continuous-data assumptions. A two-sample t test compares their means. Remember to ask who was measured, not whether the groups used the same instrument or had the same number of columns.

exhibit.title: Remaining abscess-cavity area — illustrative clinical study
exhibit.body: Invented protocol observations for an unnamed investigational topical agent in lactational breast abscesses. Outcome: remaining abscess-cavity area, in square centimeters. Two separately sampled treatment groups contribute one measurement per person. Groups do not overlap and nobody is matched. Measurements are approximately normal with comparable variability and no influential outliers. These practice assumptions supply no real treatment efficacy.

Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine Clinical Protocol #36: The Mastitis Spectrum, Revised 2022

answerChoices.rationale: The reserve conclusion needs correction, but the symptom-provoking liquid load does not itself supply evidence for the added outflow revision.

answerChoices.label: Retain the reserve conclusion; revise the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: This accepts suppression as proof of reserve and lets symptom reproduction override the actual junction and pressure observations during loading.

answerChoices.label: Revise the reserve conclusion; retain the outflow conclusion

frozenCase.displayName: Select an independent-samples t test and Select a paired t test
frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the breast-service research lead, reviews a trial of a new topical agent after drainage of lactational breast abscesses. Different participants received each preparation. Ultrasound measured the remaining cavity area at the protocol visit. A colleague proposes linking the groups because the same sonographer collected all measurements. The report includes the distribution checks for analysis.
sourceLabels: ACR Appropriateness Criteria Breast Imaging During Lactation
Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine Clinical Protocol #36: The Mastitis Spectrum, Revised 2022

decisionNodes.stem: Which analysis best fits the study's comparison of mean remaining abscess-cavity area, using the measurements and assumptions in the exhibit?

answerChoices.label: Two-sample t test
answerChoices.rationale: The study compares means from two groups of different people, and its stated continuous-data assumptions are reasonable. A two-sample t procedure matches that structure.

answerChoices.label: Wilcoxon rank-sum test
answerChoices.rationale: Rank-sum answers a ranked-observation comparison. This study explicitly requests means and supplies reasonable assumptions for the mean-based procedure.

answerChoices.label: Chi-square test of independence
answerChoices.rationale: Chi-square testing analyzes counts in categories. The requested comparison concerns continuous measurements or ordered ratings, not a categorical contingency table.

answerChoices.label: Paired t test
answerChoices.rationale: A paired t procedure needs repeated or deliberately matched measurements. This comparison does not supply those links between observations.

decisionNodes.explanation: A two-sample t test fits mean remaining abscess-cavity area in two nonoverlapping groups. Using the same sonographer does not create repeated or matched observations.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: The scanner does not define the relationship between observations. These abscess-cavity areas come from different people in two nonoverlapping groups, with suitable continuous-data assumptions. A two-sample t test compares their means. Remember to ask who was measured, not whether the groups used the same instrument or had the same number of columns.

exhibit.title: Remaining abscess-cavity area — illustrative clinical study
exhibit.body: Invented protocol observations for an unnamed investigational topical agent in lactational breast abscesses. Outcome: remaining abscess-cavity area, in square centimeters. Two separately sampled treatment groups contribute one measurement per person. Groups do not overlap and nobody is matched. Measurements are approximately normal with comparable variability and no influential outliers. These practice assumptions supply no real treatment efficacy.

sourceLabels: ACR Appropriateness Criteria Breast Imaging During Lactation
Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine Clinical Protocol #36: The Mastitis Spectrum, Revised 2022

frozenCase.displayName: Select an independent-samples t test and Select a paired t test
frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the breast-service research lead, reviews a trial of a new topical agent after drainage of lactational breast abscesses. Different participants received each preparation. Ultrasound measured the remaining cavity area at the protocol visit. A colleague proposes linking the groups because the same sonographer collected all measurements. The report includes the distribution checks for analysis.
sourceLabels: ACR Appropriateness Criteria Breast Imaging During Lactation
Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine Clinical Protocol #36: The Mastitis Spectrum, Revised 2022

decisionNodes.stem: Which analysis best fits the study's comparison of mean remaining abscess-cavity area, using the measurements and assumptions in the exhibit?

answerChoices.label: Two-sample t test
answerChoices.rationale: The study compares means from two groups of different people, and its stated continuous-data assumptions are reasonable. A two-sample t procedure matches that structure.

answerChoices.label: Wilcoxon rank-sum test
answerChoices.rationale: Rank-sum answers a ranked-observation comparison. This study explicitly requests means and supplies reasonable assumptions for the mean-based procedure.

answerChoices.label: Chi-square test of independence
answerChoices.rationale: Chi-square testing analyzes counts in categories. The requested comparison concerns continuous measurements or ordered ratings, not a categorical contingency table.

answerChoices.label: Paired t test
answerChoices.rationale: A paired t procedure needs repeated or deliberately matched measurements. This comparison does not supply those links between observations.

decisionNodes.explanation: A two-sample t test fits mean remaining abscess-cavity area in two nonoverlapping groups. Using the same sonographer does not create repeated or matched observations.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: The scanner does not define the relationship between observations. These abscess-cavity areas come from different people in two nonoverlapping groups, with suitable continuous-data assumptions. A two-sample t test compares their means. Remember to ask who was measured, not whether the groups used the same instrument or had the same number of columns.

exhibit.title: Remaining abscess-cavity area — illustrative clinical study
exhibit.body: Invented protocol observations for an unnamed investigational topical agent in lactational breast abscesses. Outcome: remaining abscess-cavity area, in square centimeters. Two separately sampled treatment groups contribute one measurement per person. Groups do not overlap and nobody is matched. Measurements are approximately normal with comparable variability and no influential outliers. These practice assumptions supply no real treatment efficacy.

decisionNodes.stem: What should the team disclose to Owen Garner about the verified unintended enterotomy during incisional-hernia repair?

answerChoices.label: Explain that review must finish before discussing events
answerChoices.rationale: An internal review may clarify remaining uncertainties, but it does not require withholding the verified injury and repair. Known facts and the care plan can be discussed now.

answerChoices.label: Explain the planned care without mentioning the injury
answerChoices.rationale: A forward-looking care plan does not replace an honest account of the verified operative event. The patient has asked why the operation changed.

answerChoices.label: Explain the repair and leave its cause unstated
answerChoices.rationale: Describing the repair alone omits the verified error that prompted it. A technically true fragment can still leave the patient with a misleading account.

answerChoices.label: Explain the operative error and continuing care plan
answerChoices.rationale: Explain the verified unintended injury, its repair, known implications and continuing care plan honestly. Reporting the repair alone would conceal why the operation changed.

decisionNodes.explanation: Explain the verified unintended injury, its repair, known implications and continuing care plan. An incomplete account or unfinished internal review does not justify concealing known facts.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Honest disclosure explains the verified error, its known implications and the steps taken to address it. Here that includes the unintended bowel injury, repair and continuing care plan. Remember: separate known facts from remaining uncertainty. A description of the repair alone can mislead if it conceals why the operation changed.

decisionNodes.stem: What should the team explain when Julia Walton is told that ordinary gastric-GIST care depends on joining an optional new-biologic study?

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment limits access to routine follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Limiting routine follow-up uses ordinary care to pressure enrollment. The optional study is not required for that care.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment does not forfeit ordinary care
answerChoices.rationale: This study is optional and not required for ordinary care. Clarify that declining enrollment does not forfeit that care, so the invitation can be considered voluntarily.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment requires transfer to another clinic
answerChoices.rationale: Requiring transfer would impose a loss of ordinary care for declining this optional study. The scenario gives no basis for making that care contingent on enrollment.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment postpones the surgical consultation
answerChoices.rationale: Postponing the ordinary consultation because enrollment is declined still makes care conditional on joining. That conflicts with voluntary choice in this setting.

decisionNodes.explanation: Clarify that declining this optional study does not forfeit ordinary clinic care. The recruiter's stated condition is inconsistent with voluntary participation in a study not required for that care.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Research participation must be voluntary. When a study is optional and not required for ordinary care, declining it should not forfeit that care. Remember to separate the clinical care decision from the research invitation. Making enrollment a condition of routine care pressures the patient instead of supporting an independent choice about participation.
sourceLabels: 2023 GEIS Guidelines for gastrointestinal stromal tumors
Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors Treatment (PDQ®), Health Professional Version

decisionNodes.stem: Which multidisciplinary treatment plan best fits Julia Walton's imatinib-sensitive, nonmetastatic gastric GIST when tumor shrinkage could reduce the morbidity of the planned extensive resection?

answerChoices.label: Give neoadjuvant cytotoxic chemotherapy before resection
answerChoices.rationale: Conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy is not the selected targeted approach for imatinib-sensitive GIST.

answerChoices.label: Plan neoadjuvant imatinib before reassessing resection
answerChoices.rationale: For an imatinib-sensitive GIST where the multidisciplinary team expects shrinkage to reduce operative morbidity, neoadjuvant imatinib with later resection reassessment is appropriate; size alone would not establish this plan.

answerChoices.label: Offer symptom-directed care without tumor treatment
answerChoices.rationale: Symptom-only care does not address this large, locally advanced lesion.

answerChoices.label: Proceed directly to the planned extensive resection
answerChoices.rationale: Immediate extensive surgery gives up the documented opportunity for morbidity-reducing shrinkage.

decisionNodes.explanation: Plan neoadjuvant imatinib with later reassessment of resection for this mutation-sensitive GIST. The documented opportunity to reduce operative morbidity supports the plan; size alone does not.

decisionNodes.stem: Which change should be requested in Samuel Quincy's draft report?

answerChoices.label: Retain the reserve conclusion; revise the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: This accepts suppression as proof of reserve and lets symptom reproduction override the actual junction and pressure observations during loading.

answerChoices.label: Retain the reserve conclusion; retain the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: Baseline propagation and appropriate inhibition do not establish the post-sequence reserve response. Accepting the whole draft misses that distinction.

answerChoices.label: Revise the reserve conclusion; retain the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: Normal inhibition during the sequence is not evidence of post-sequence augmentation. The repeat responses challenge the reserve conclusion, whereas reproduced discomfort without the supplied outflow findings does not establish liquid-load obstruction.

answerChoices.label: Revise the reserve conclusion; revise the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: The reserve conclusion needs correction, but the symptom-provoking liquid load does not itself supply evidence for the added outflow revision.

decisionNodes.explanation: A provocative protocol has distinct acquisition phases. A familiar symptom during rapid drinking does not by itself establish impaired outflow. This report review does not assign a final motor diagnosis or a cause of all symptoms.

frozenCase.displayName: Select an independent-samples t test and Select a paired t test
frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the breast-service research lead, reviews a trial of a new topical agent after drainage of lactational breast abscesses. Different participants received each preparation. Ultrasound measured the remaining cavity area at the protocol visit. A colleague proposes linking the groups because the same sonographer collected all measurements. The report includes the distribution checks for analysis.
sourceLabels: ACR Appropriateness Criteria Breast Imaging During Lactation
Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine Clinical Protocol #36: The Mastitis Spectrum, Revised 2022

decisionNodes.stem: Which analysis best fits the study's comparison of mean remaining abscess-cavity area, using the measurements and assumptions in the exhibit?

answerChoices.label: Two-sample t test
answerChoices.rationale: The study compares means from two groups of different people, and its stated continuous-data assumptions are reasonable. A two-sample t procedure matches that structure.

answerChoices.label: Wilcoxon rank-sum test
answerChoices.rationale: Rank-sum answers a ranked-observation comparison. This study explicitly requests means and supplies reasonable assumptions for the mean-based procedure.

answerChoices.label: Chi-square test of independence
answerChoices.rationale: Chi-square testing analyzes counts in categories. The requested comparison concerns continuous measurements or ordered ratings, not a categorical contingency table.

answerChoices.label: Paired t test
answerChoices.rationale: A paired t procedure needs repeated or deliberately matched measurements. This comparison does not supply those links between observations.

decisionNodes.explanation: A two-sample t test fits mean remaining abscess-cavity area in two nonoverlapping groups. Using the same sonographer does not create repeated or matched observations.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: The scanner does not define the relationship between observations. These abscess-cavity areas come from different people in two nonoverlapping groups, with suitable continuous-data assumptions. A two-sample t test compares their means. Remember to ask who was measured, not whether the groups used the same instrument or had the same number of columns.

exhibit.title: Remaining abscess-cavity area — illustrative clinical study
exhibit.body: Invented protocol observations for an unnamed investigational topical agent in lactational breast abscesses. Outcome: remaining abscess-cavity area, in square centimeters. Two separately sampled treatment groups contribute one measurement per person. Groups do not overlap and nobody is matched. Measurements are approximately normal with comparable variability and no influential outliers. These practice assumptions supply no real treatment efficacy.

sourceLabels: ACR Appropriateness Criteria Breast Imaging During Lactation
Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine Clinical Protocol #36: The Mastitis Spectrum, Revised 2022

decisionNodes.stem: What should the team explain when Julia Walton is told that ordinary gastric-GIST care depends on joining an optional new-biologic study?

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment limits access to routine follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Limiting routine follow-up uses ordinary care to pressure enrollment. The optional study is not required for that care.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment does not forfeit ordinary care
answerChoices.rationale: This study is optional and not required for ordinary care. Clarify that declining enrollment does not forfeit that care, so the invitation can be considered voluntarily.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment requires transfer to another clinic
answerChoices.rationale: Requiring transfer would impose a loss of ordinary care for declining this optional study. The scenario gives no basis for making that care contingent on enrollment.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment postpones the surgical consultation
answerChoices.rationale: Postponing the ordinary consultation because enrollment is declined still makes care conditional on joining. That conflicts with voluntary choice in this setting.

decisionNodes.explanation: Clarify that declining this optional study does not forfeit ordinary clinic care. The recruiter's stated condition is inconsistent with voluntary participation in a study not required for that care.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Research participation must be voluntary. When a study is optional and not required for ordinary care, declining it should not forfeit that care. decisionNodes.stem: Which change should be requested in Samuel Quincy's draft report?

answerChoices.label: Retain the reserve conclusion; revise the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: This accepts suppression as proof of reserve and lets symptom reproduction override the actual junction and pressure observations during loading.

answerChoices.label: Retain the reserve conclusion; retain the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: Baseline propagation and appropriate inhibition do not establish the post-sequence reserve response. Accepting the whole draft misses that distinction.

answerChoices.label: Revise the reserve conclusion; retain the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: Normal inhibition during the sequence is not evidence of post-sequence augmentation. The repeat responses challenge the reserve conclusion, whereas reproduced discomfort without the supplied outflow findings does not establish liquid-load obstruction.

answerChoices.label: Revise the reserve conclusion; revise the outflow conclusion

decisionNodes.explanation: The failed/premature body activity with impaired junction relaxation is an achalasia-like spastic pattern. Opioids can produce this phenotype; Chicago v4 advises studying off opioids when possible. Coordinate a clinically appropriate withdrawal/reassessment plan before treating this as established primary disease requiring myotomy. No abrupt cessation or fixed washout is prescribed.

decisionNodes.stem: Which treatment plan should be discussed for Grace Winter's resection site?

answerChoices.label: Segmental colectomy with removal of the draining mesentery
answerChoices.rationale: Interprets the adverse invasive-polyp feature and recognizes a regional-node risk that a clear-looking scar or negative CT cannot remove.

decisionNodes.explanation: An endoscopically removed malignant polyp is not automatically cured by a clear-looking scar. Exact bowel extent, especially for a transverse lesion, remains an anatomic operative decision.

frozenCase.displayName: Select an independent-samples t test and Select a paired t test
frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the breast-service research lead, reviews a trial of a new topical agent after drainage of lactational breast abscesses. Different participants received each preparation. Ultrasound measured the remaining cavity area at the protocol visit. A colleague proposes linking the groups because the same sonographer collected all measurements. The report includes the distribution checks for analysis.
sourceLabels: ACR Appropriateness Criteria Breast Imaging During Lactation
Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine Clinical Protocol #36: The Mastitis Spectrum, Revised 2022

decisionNodes.stem: Which analysis best fits the study's comparison of mean remaining abscess-cavity area, using the measurements and assumptions in the exhibit?

answerChoices.label: Two-sample t test
answerChoices.rationale: The study compares means from two groups of different people, and its stated continuous-data assumptions are reasonable. A two-sample t procedure matches that structure.

answerChoices.label: Wilcoxon rank-sum test
answerChoices.rationale: Rank-sum answers a ranked-observation comparison. This study explicitly requests means and supplies reasonable assumptions for the mean-based procedure.

answerChoices.label: Chi-square test of independence
answerChoices.rationale: Chi-square testing analyzes counts in categories. The requested comparison concerns continuous measurements or ordered ratings, not a categorical contingency table.

answerChoices.label: Paired t test
answerChoices.rationale: A paired t procedure needs repeated or deliberately matched measurements. This comparison does not supply those links between observations.

decisionNodes.explanation: A two-sample t test fits mean remaining abscess-cavity area in two nonoverlapping groups. Using the same sonographer does not create repeated or matched observations.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: The scanner does not define the relationship between observations. These abscess-cavity areas come from different people in two nonoverlapping groups, with suitable continuous-data assumptions. A two-sample t test compares their means. Remember to ask who was measured, not whether the groups used the same instrument or had the same number of columns.

exhibit.title: Remaining abscess-cavity area — illustrative clinical study
exhibit.body: Invented protocol observations for an unnamed investigational topical agent in lactational breast abscesses. Outcome: remaining abscess-cavity area, in square centimeters. Two separately sampled treatment groups contribute one measurement per person. Groups do not overlap and nobody is matched. Measurements are approximately normal with comparable variability and no influential outliers. These practice assumptions supply no real treatment efficacy.

Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine Clinical Protocol #36: The Mastitis Spectrum, Revised 2022

categories.formula: Mean per-minute effective morale of all employed staff; empty workforce = 0
categories.improvementHint: Pay wages, use praise/coffee, complete breaks and management rounds, and retain honest ownership support.

categories.formula: Sum of final scored-patient satisfaction / all scored completions and walkouts in the window
categories.improvementHint: Answer correctly, attend patients promptly and keep facilities clean and accessible. Use actual garden/Executive comfort; walkouts stay in the sample.

categories.formula: 100 × [0.5 × (1 − overdue queue-minutes / queue-minutes) + 0.5 × completed / (completed + walkouts)]
categories.improvementHint: Staff check-in, maintain paths/seats/care capacity and answer ready questions. Prescribed processing, travel and external-result clocks are excluded.

categories.formula: 100 × [0.5 × fully paid positive bills / positive bills + 0.5 × clip(operating net / (0.05 × operating gross))]
categories.improvementHint: Pay every bill and build real profitable services within demand. Stock is deducted once; capital spending, reserves, grants and room sales cannot improve operating profit.

categories.formula: 100 × correct first submissions / (all first submissions + presented but unanswered questions)
categories.improvementHint: Review existing explanations and answer every presented game question correctly. Wrong first answers and unanswered questions remain; this compares stored game keys, not real clinical competence.
